To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current state-of-the-art models are the sequence to sequence models with the re-parametrization techniques, which are able to generate high quality and diverse text.
the generative adversarial net based text generator performs best among the models we tested, and that the GPT-2 text generator is the only one that can generate text that is not repetitive.

(a) RNNs with maximum likelihood estimation training are not suitable for text generation because of gradient vanishing and lack of generation diversity; (b) reinforcement learning, re-parameterization tricks and GANs can be used to address these issues; (c) the re-parameterization tricks can be applied to all the three types of models, but the GANs and reinforcement learning can not be applied to the re-parameterization models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic study and evaluation of recent neural text generation methods, which will be beneficial for both the research community and the industry.
the development of neural text generators that can generate fluent and diverse texts.
the recent development of neural network models and the corresponding learning algorithms for natural language processing (NLP) tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neural text generation has been a hot topic recently, and it will continue to be in the near future.
the GAN-based models are the most promising ones in terms of generation quality and diversity.
the recent neural text generation models have achieved promising progress and the future research directions are promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current state-of-the-art neural text generation model is the GAN-based model.
the recent development of neural language models has made great progress in text generation.

the current state-of-the-art neural text generation methods can be roughly categorized into three types: (i) RNN language model with re-parametrization techniques; (ii) RNN language models with policy gradient methods; and (iii) GAN-based text generation models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the recently proposed techniques can be used to alleviate some of the common problems in neural text generation, such as gradient vanishaing and generation diversity, and that the performance of these models can be further improved by incorporating more advanced techniques.
there is no one-size-fits-all model for all text generation applications.
, although the current state-of-the-art text generation models are capable of generating fluent text, they still have a long way to go before they can produce high-quality and diverse texts.
